Lauren / Ben — quick technical summary from triage (I looked at the pcap and logs):

Findings:
- There was no control-plane rollout during the 00:00-02:00 UTC window; control plane was stable.
- MedNexus applied kernel patches locally Saturday night (per their note), but the captured traffic shows the agent initiating TLS renegotiation on long-lived control sockets which leads to a keepalive timer mismatch in our current agent 1.18.2 when combined with certain kernel TCP timeout behaviors.
- Symptoms: three-way handshake completes, TLS renegotiation begins, agent's keepalive probe is reset incorrectly which the control plane treats as a connection drop. This explains the short blips and subsequent automatic fallback.

Immediate mitigation applied (within 50 minutes of report):
1) We pushed a temporary agent config tweak for MedNexus to increase the keepalive interval and enable explicit TCP keepalive probes (recommended values: tcp_keepalive_time=120, tcp_keepalive_intvl=10). MedNexus applied this and we saw connection stability improve.
2) For customers on agent 1.18.2 we published a targeted patch to disable in-process TLS renegotiation until a proper fix lands. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/3921 (patch linked).

Next steps / timeline:
- Ship a tested agent binary (1.18.3) with the TLS renegotiation fix and stronger socket handling by 2028-01-24 18:00 UTC (target). Patch branch and patch file attached.
- Postmortem doc with timeline and recommended network/kernel guidance for customers by 2028-01-25 EOD.
- Recommend we offer a 1-week credit for MedNexus given production impact; Ben, can you coordinate commercial?

I'll follow with the patch artifact and a short runbook for customers who cannot upgrade immediately.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-incident update and next steps — MedNexus control-link blips

Hi Sara,

Thanks again for the packet captures and for working quickly with our on-call team. Below is a concise summary and the remediation plan. Please let me know if you'd like a call to walk through the timelines.

What happened
- Short control-plane connection drops were observed on 2028-01-22 ~01:15 UTC for a subset of agent nodes in MedNexus's private deployment. The drops caused automatic fallback to Redwood hosted endpoints for ~18 minutes total across affected shards.

Root cause
- Our investigation indicates an interaction between agent TLS renegotiation on long-lived control sockets and certain kernel TCP keepalive behavior after MedNexus's Saturday kernel patches. Agent 1.18.2 has a keepalive/renegotiation handling gap that in edge cases can present as a connection drop.

Actions taken
- Immediate: Config knob recommended (tcp_keepalive_time=120, tcp_keepalive_intvl=10) which MedNexus applied; stability returned.
- Short-term: We published a targeted configuration/patch and disabled in-process TLS renegotiation for affected agents.
- Medium-term: Ship agent 1.18.3 with a full fix and hardening of socket handling (target 2028-01-24). Patch and PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/3921
- Documentation: We prepared a customer-specific runbook and a postmortem (attached).

Compensation and commercial next steps
- Redwood is proposing a one-week service credit for the affected capacity while you were on fallback; Ben will follow up to coordinate.

Attachments
- mednexus_20280122_control_link_pcap.pcap (pcap)
- redwood_agent_fix_1_18_3.patch (diff)
- mednexus_controllink_postmortem_20280125.docx (postmortem)

If you approve, we'll schedule a 30-minute technical review with your IT team and our SREs to go over the postmortem and the upgrade plan.

Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this with the highest priority and will update you if anything else is discovered.

Best regards,
